top news.title: Anthropic debuts Claude Fable 5, a “safe” Mythos-class model it says can't be used for cyberattacks, to the public, and Claude Mythos 5 to trusted organizations

tweets.author: @karpathy
tweets.text: This is a super exciting release - Claude Fable 5 is the same underlying model as Mythos but with added safeguards.  The benchmarks are great and it's SOTA on everything by a margin but I'll add that *qualitatively* also, this is a major-version-bump-deserving step change forward...peaking especially for long problem-solving sessions on very difficult problems...The model still has quirks that people will run into and the safeguards are configured to be a little too trigger happy for launch, which can hopefully be tuned over time.

tweets.author: @bcherny
tweets.text: Fable 5 is the biggest step up I've felt in our models since Opus 4.5 back in November.  After 4.5 came out I uninstalled my IDE when I realized that I'd been doing 100% of my coding in a terminal for a few weeks.  With Fable, it's felt like Claude has stepped up from being a coding agent to a thought and design partner in building the product.  Fable has judgement, taste, and dimensionality in a way that previous models didn't, leading me to trust it more with the most complex work

tweets.author: @yuchenj_uw
tweets.text: Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5 wins everywhere.  I thought Fable 5 was just a nerfed Mythos Preview, but it's literally better.  SWE-Bench Pro: Fable 5: 80.3%, GPT-5.5: 58.6%.  And the price is only 2x Opus 4.8: $10/input MTok, $50/output MTok.  I don't think GPT 5.6 can beat this

sub_items.title: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5 uses conservative safety classifiers that trigger a fallback to Claude Opus 4.8 in <5% of sessions, in areas like cybersecurity
Anthropic says Fable 5 has invisible safeguards that use prompt modification, steering vectors, or PEFT to limit its effectiveness for building frontier LLMs
Anthropic prices both Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 at $10 per 1M input tokens and $50 per 1M output tokens, less than half the price of Claude Mythos Preview
Anthropic says Fable 5 is available on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans through June 22, after which using Fable 5 will require usage credits
Claude Fable 5 hands-on: impressive results working on complex projects, like building an interactive isochrone map or a data analysis tool in just 9.5 hours
Anthropic says red team tests of Fable 5 found no universal jailbreaks, and it will keep first- and third-party user traffic on Mythos-class models for 30 days

top news.title: The EU says Apple decided not to roll out Siri AI in the EU after it had unsuccessfully requested to be exempted from interoperability obligations for the tool

tweets.author: @jewiss
tweets.text: Apple and the EU are telling very different stories on Siri AI, and right now, it's a standoff.  Apple's press release and comments to @LelloucheNico say the DMA would force it to give rival assistants deep access to messages, files, photos, app actions, and personal context, creating privacy/security risks.  I reached out to the EU Commission for comment...They said nothing in the DMA blocks Siri AI.  Apple can launch it if it complies, but it must give rivals “equivalent access” and can't use iOS to favour its own AI.

tweets.author: @electric_maik
tweets.text: Apple is currently holding back Siri AI within the EU because the company is a designated gatekeeper under the Digital Markets Act.  For roughly 18 months, Apple has been trying to find a way to bring the new Siri AI to Europe while complying with DMA rules.  Apple proposed a solution called the „Trusted System Agent"...However, the European Commission rejected all of Apple's proposals.

tweets.author: @timsweeneyepic
tweets.text: @Electric_Maik They dissuaded 60% of Epic Games customers from installing our store after they started the process. The EU found that unlawful and forced Apple to change, and they did. Trust the rule of law here to bring competition to Siri, currently the industry's worst AI assistant.

top news.title: Google and Nvidia are helping Apple with Apple Foundation Model Cloud Pro, which Apple says is comparable to Gemini frontier models and runs on Nvidia GPUs

tweets.author: @awnihannun
tweets.text: It's very cool that Apple shipped a 20B parameter on-device.  You can't put 20B parameters in RAM at any reasonable precision.  To make it work they are using pretty exotic architecture by today's standards.  A small model predicts from the query (or prompt) which experts to load from Nand into RAM.  The key distinction from a typical MoE is that you do this once per query and then generate all the tokens with the same experts (instead of switching the experts for every token).

tweets.author: @mweinbach
tweets.text: Apple just clarified AFM Cloud is Apple's own model, trained with Gemini outputs AFM local models are entirely Apple models AFM Cloud Pro seems to be based on Gemini foundation and data, but Apple did their own pre-training, post-training, RL, etc

tweets.author: @benbajarin
tweets.text: Apple execs confirming using broader GCP and NVIDIA GPUs for Apple Private cloud compute: “This is our most capable model, with quality similar to Gemini Frontier models, and to bring this model to production, we work with both Google and Nvidia to extend our private cloud compute infrastructure to Nvidia GPUs in Google's cloud, while maintaining Apple's unmatched privacy guarantees.”
